blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) in Mimaropa is studying the reproductive biology of the octopus Octopus cyanea, locally known as “pugita,” to generate scientific data that could support sustainable fisheries management in the region, according to a social media post on Wednesday, Sept. 30. The assessment, which began in July 2026 under BFAR Mimaropa’s National Stock Assessment Program (NSAP), is part of a comprehensive profiling and biological assessment of octopus marine farms in the country’s five major octopus-producing regions.
